items.title: Show HN: I built an agent-first productivity bridge for all your agents
items.why_it_matters: An indie designer-turned-developer built TaskShell, a productivity bridge designed to track tasks and todos directly across different coding agents like Claude Code and Codex. They built it to solve the exact context-switching friction of repeating todo lists to different agents. You can sign up for the tool this week and use it to manage your AI-ingest roadmap directly inside your active Claude Code terminal.

items.title: Show HN: Wattage – finds the tokens your Claude Code sessions wasted
items.why_it_matters: A new tool called Wattage analyzes your local Claude Code history to identify exactly where and how you are wasting tokens and money. Since you are actively using Claude Code, this is a direct way to keep your development costs down. You can clone the GitHub repo today and run it against your local Claude Code log directory to see your token waste.

items.title: Show HN: Agent-hop – a Rust TUI that hops a live Claude Code chat into Codex
items.why_it_matters: Agent-hop is a terminal UI that lets you hop a live chat session between different coding agents like Claude Code and Codex without losing your current context. This solves the friction of starting from scratch when you want to switch models. You can install this TUI today and use it to hop a tricky Next.js bug-fixing session from Claude Code over to Codex to see how they compare.

items.title: Serve Markdown to AI Agents with Accept Headers
items.why_it_matters: This guide introduces a simple pattern: serving clean, LLM-friendly markdown from your web apps by detecting 'Accept: text/markdown' headers. This is incredibly useful for your AI-ingest project, as it allows agents to read your site's content without HTML clutter. You can implement this header check in your Next.js API routes this week so you can easily curl clean markdown directly into Claude Code.

items.title: WebMCP: Teaching Your Website to Talk to AI Agents
items.why_it_matters: WebMCP is a new lightweight library that lets you easily expose Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoints directly from your website. This means you can turn your web app's database or APIs into tools that external AI agents can use. You can plug this into your Next.js AI-ingest project this week to let your local Claude Code agent query your Supabase database directly.
